chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam and Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, all from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every supplication with which Allah (Exalted and Majestic) is supplicated is veiled from the sky until blessings are sent upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
ai.seo_question: Why are supplications considered veiled before sending blessings upon the Prophet?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Safwan al-Jammal narrates from Imam al-Sadiq (as) that every supplication remains veiled from the heavens until preceded by blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, establishing salawat as a spiritual key for du'a acceptance. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that salawat serves not merely as etiquette but as a necessary condition for the spiritual ascent of prayers, linking the supplicant directly to the divine through the Prophet's intercessory status.
